name: commercetools
_readme: commercetools Composable Commerce as a TARGET only: multi-tenant, API-first SaaS on GCP with NO built-in frontend, NO CMS, NO order-management UI and NO search-merchandising UI - everything above the API is built or bought. Extension happens through API Extensions, Subscriptions, Custom Applications in the Merchant Center and Connect connectors, so there is no shop code base to inventory. Seed from stable API-shape knowledge. No source role, no adapter.py.

as_target.default_frontend: none shipped - commercetools Frontend (formerly Frontastic) or a custom frontend (Next.js/React, Vue Storefront, Vercel Commerce)

snippets.critic2_persona: senior solution architect who has delivered several commercetools Composable Commerce programmes, is commercetools-certified, and is disciplined about the platform boundary - what the API guarantees, what the Merchant Center actually offers a business user, and which capability has to be a separate product in the composable stack
snippets.docs_domains: docs.commercetools.com (the HTTP API reference per resource, GraphQL API, Import API, Subscriptions, API Extensions, Custom Applications, Merchant Center, the Checkout and Frontend products, and the update-action catalogue per resource - update actions are the real API contract, read them, not the resource description); docs.commercetools.com/api/limits for the per-project limits and quotas and docs.commercetools.com/api/general-concepts for eventual consistency and reference expansion; commercetools.com/connect and the Connect marketplace for pre-built connectors; github.com/commercetools (official SDKs for Java, TypeScript/JavaScript, PHP, .NET, Python, and the commercetools Frontend / Composable Commerce examples); docs.commercetools.com/sdk for SDK behaviour. Product names shift (Frontastic became commercetools Frontend, Composable Commerce is the platform brand) - cite the current page, never a remembered product name.
snippets.best_practice: model the domain with the platform's own primitives before reaching for custom fields: Product Types for attributes, Types for custom fields on any resource, Channels for supply and distribution, Stores for market/brand separation, Product Selections for assortments, Standalone Prices for large price volumes, States for lifecycle; drive every write through the documented update actions on the resource version (optimistic concurrency - always send the current version and handle 409 by re-reading); never read the write model for a storefront listing, use the Product Search / product-projections search endpoint and accept that it is eventually consistent; put custom synchronous logic in an API Extension only where it must block the request and keep it inside the extension timeout, everything else belongs on a Subscription with an idempotent consumer; keep the Merchant Center usable for the business by adding Custom Applications instead of building a second admin, and treat missing back-office UIs (order management, merchandising, content) as products to select, not as gaps to code away.
snippets.critic2_focus: D1: current product and feature names (Composable Commerce, Frontend, Checkout, Connect, Product Search), which capability is GA versus beta, and the per-project limits and quotas that apply. D2: is the claimed standard capability really a platform resource with update actions, or is it a Connect connector, a partner product or bespoke code. D3: does the API really cover the requirement END TO END including the ADMIN side - a capability that exists on the API but has no Merchant Center screen is not covered for a business user, say so explicitly. D4: exact resource paths, update-action names and GraphQL fields; whether the read path is the write model or the eventually consistent search projection; and for every content requirement, which external CMS provides the component and how it is bound to catalog data.
snippets.expected_hotspots_d3: content and landing pages of any kind (no CMS - see content_model_notes); order management and fulfilment operations for CSR and warehouse staff (no OMS UI); search merchandising and ranking rules (no merchandising UI in the standard - verify the current Product Search / Search Merchandising status); promotions beyond cart discounts, product discounts and discount codes (complex bundle, gift-with-purchase and coupon-hierarchy logic); contract and customer-specific pricing at large volume (Standalone Prices, price tiers, channel/store scoping and the resulting price-selection rules); tax determination beyond tax categories and rates (external tax engine); returns, credit notes and invoicing documents; punchout (OCI / cXML); customer service tooling and impersonation; approval flows deeper than the shipped Business Unit / Associate Role model; product data authoring at scale, which usually means an external PIM
snippets.expected_blockers_d4: there is NO CMS - every page, banner, navigation entry and editorial block needs an external CMS plus a binding layer, and the CMS choice becomes part of the target architecture; there is NO order-management UI and NO search-merchandising UI in the standard, so back-office capability that a legacy platform provided for free becomes a product selection or a custom Merchant Center Custom Application; product-projections / Product Search are eventually consistent projections of the write model, so read-after-write in a storefront flow, and any assumption that a price or availability change is instantly searchable, will break; everything above the API is your own frontend, your own SSR/caching strategy and your own SEO and URL model (no built-in URL resolver beyond slugs); API Extensions run synchronously inside a request with a hard timeout and must be highly available or writes fail, so validation-heavy legacy logic cannot simply move there; Subscriptions are at-least-once and unordered, so every consumer must be idempotent; per-project API limits and quotas (request rate, resource counts, query and search restrictions, reference-expansion depth) shape the integration design; optimistic concurrency on every write (version + 409) has to be handled everywhere, which legacy integration code usually does not do; no built-in CSR/impersonation, no built-in document generation, and data migration must run through the Import API with its own asynchronous semantics
snippets.content_model_notes: commercetools ships NO CMS. There is no page, no template, no slot, no block and no content-versioning resource in the platform - the only content-shaped things are localized fields and Assets on catalog resources (product, product variant, category), Type-based custom fields on any resource, and CustomObjects as an untyped JSON store that projects sometimes abuse as a content or configuration container. Consequence for a fit estimation: EVERY content, landing-page, banner, navigation and editorial requirement is met by an external system (a headless CMS such as Contentful, Contentstack, Storyblok, Amplience, Sanity, or commercetools Frontend's own page/tastic model), plus the integration that binds CMS components to catalog data and the frontend that renders them. commercetools Frontend (formerly Frontastic) provides page folders, page templates and tastics (frontend components bound to data sources) and is the closest thing to a first-party answer, but it is a separate product with its own licence and its own component model *(verify its current scope)*. Never record a content requirement as covered-standard on this platform: state the CMS, the binding and the renderer as three distinct pieces of work.
snippets.api_families_hint: see knowledge target_api_endpoint_families - one uniform surface per project (https://api.<region>.commercetools.com/<projectKey>/<resource>) available as both HTTP/REST and GraphQL, with a separate auth host for OAuth2 tokens, a separate Import API host for bulk loads, and the update-action catalogue per resource as the actual write contract
